configs.title: Root-to-tip clock regression (dengue/100).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-clock.schema.json

# Root-to-tip clock regression (dengue/100).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime clock --config data/dengue/100/clock.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/dengue/100/clock
#
# `clock` reroots the tree to maximize the temporal signal, then fits the
# root-to-tip regression and reports the clock rate. The taxon identifier lives
# in a non-default metadata column here, named once in the config instead of a
# `--metadata-id-columns genbank_accession` flag repeated on every run.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
metadata_id_columns:
  - "genbank_accession"

configs.title: Branch-length optimization in the dense representation (dengue/1000).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-optimize.schema.json

# Branch-length optimization in the dense representation (dengue/1000).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime optimize --config data/dengue/1000/optimize-dense.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/dengue/1000/optimize-dense
#
# `optimize` alternates marginal reconstruction and per-branch length updates. In
# the dense representation (`representation: dense`) every pass keeps the state
# probabilities of all sites at all nodes, so each iteration costs much more than
# in the sparse representation that the default chooses. The run reroots on the
# minimum-divergence branch.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

representation: "dense"
reroot: "min-dev"

configs.title: Ancestral reconstruction by Fitch parsimony (ebola/20).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-ancestral.schema.json

# Ancestral reconstruction by Fitch parsimony (ebola/20).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime ancestral --config data/ebola/20/ancestral-parsimony.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/ebola/20/ancestral-parsimony
#
# A per-command config is the command's own argument object. Every value here
# has a matching `--flag`; the file is a saved, reviewable, version-controlled
# invocation. An explicit flag on the command line still overrides the file.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

# Fitch parsimony: fast, model-free ancestral states and mutations.
method_anc: "parsimony"

configs.title: Time tree with a skyline coalescent in the dense representation (ebola/362).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-timetree.schema.json

# Time tree with a skyline coalescent in the dense representation (ebola/362).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime timetree --config data/ebola/362/timetree-dense.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/ebola/362/timetree-dense
#
# Every timetree iteration reconstructs the ancestral sequences again. With
# `representation: dense` these reconstructions keep the state probabilities of
# every site of the 19 kb genomes at every node. The skyline coalescent
# (`coalescent: skyline`) fits a piecewise-linear history of the coalescent time
# scale Tc over the 2014-2016 West African epidemic, and `confidence` adds the 90%
# intervals of the node dates, including the uncertainty of the estimated clock
# rate. `seed` makes the random order of the polytomy resolution reproducible.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

representation: "dense"
coalescent: "skyline"
confidence: true
seed: 42

configs.title: Branch-length optimization with divergence-based rerooting (flu/h3n2/20).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-optimize.schema.json

# Branch-length optimization with divergence-based rerooting (flu/h3n2/20).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime optimize --config data/flu/h3n2/20/optimize.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/flu/h3n2/20/optimize
#
# `optimize` re-estimates every branch length under the substitution model and
# (here) reroots to minimize root-to-tip divergence variance. This is the
# date-free step that replaces `augur refine` in a Nextstrain build.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

# Per-edge optimizer: Brent's method in sqrt(t) space (the default, matches v0).
optimizer: "brent"

# Reroot by minimizing root-to-tip divergence variance (a date-free method).
reroot: "min-dev"

configs.title: Time-scaled tree with a fixed clock rate and date confidence intervals (flu/h3n2/200).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-timetree.schema.json

# Time-scaled tree with a fixed clock rate and date confidence intervals (flu/h3n2/200).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime timetree --config data/flu/h3n2/200/timetree.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/flu/h3n2/200/timetree
#
# `timetree` turns divergence into calendar time. Fixing the clock rate
# (`clock_rate`) skips rate estimation and is common for well-characterized
# pathogens like seasonal influenza. `confidence` adds date confidence
# intervals, which need a rate uncertainty (`clock_std_dev`) when the rate is
# fixed; `coalescent: opt` fits a constant coalescent time scale analytically.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

clock_rate: 0.003
clock_std_dev: 0.0006
confidence: true
coalescent: "opt"
max_iter: 3

# The default outputs: with `confidence`, the node dates table holds the 90% intervals.
output_selection:
  - "nwk"
  - "nexus"
  - "auspice"
  - "node-data"
  - "model"
  - "sequences"
  - "clock-model"
  - "coalescent"
  - "dates"

configs.title: Influenza H3N2 time tree with an estimated clock and a skyline coalescent (flu/h3n2/500).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-timetree.schema.json

# Influenza H3N2 time tree with an estimated clock and a skyline coalescent (flu/h3n2/500).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime timetree --config data/flu/h3n2/500/timetree.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/flu/h3n2/500/timetree
#
# `data/flu/h3n2/500/pipeline.yaml` fixes the clock rate; this file estimates it
# from 500 hemagglutinin sequences instead. The skyline coalescent
# (`coalescent: skyline`) fits a piecewise-linear history of the coalescent time
# scale Tc. `confidence` runs a final marginal round of the time inference and
# writes the 90% interval of every node date, including the uncertainty of the
# estimated rate. `seed` makes the random order of the polytomy resolution
# reproducible.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

coalescent: "skyline"
confidence: true
max_iter: 3
seed: 42

configs.title: Lassa virus time tree with a relaxed clock (lassa/L/500).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-timetree.schema.json

# Lassa virus time tree with a relaxed clock (lassa/L/500).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime timetree --config data/lassa/L/500/timetree.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/lassa/L/500/timetree
#
# Lassa virus circulates in rodents across West Africa and its lineages are
# centuries old, so the rate of evolution can differ between lineages. `relax`
# lets every branch have its own rate around the mean clock rate: the first value
# is the strength of the prior on the rate deviation of a branch, the second the
# coupling between the rates of parent and child branches (0 gives an
# uncorrelated clock). `coalescent: opt` fits a constant coalescent time scale, and
# `seed` makes the random order of the polytomy resolution reproducible. The taxon
# names are in the `accession` column; the 500 sequences are of the L segment.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
metadata_id_columns:
  - "accession"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

relax:
  - 1.0
  - 0.5
coalescent: "opt"
confidence: true
max_iter: 3
seed: 42

configs.title: Branch-length optimization for a Nextstrain mpox build (mpox/clade-ii/1000).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-optimize.schema.json

# Branch-length optimization for a Nextstrain mpox build (mpox/clade-ii/1000).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime optimize --config data/mpox/clade-ii/1000/optimize.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/mpox/clade-ii/1000/optimize
#
# This is the date-free step that replaces `augur refine` in the nextstrain/mpox
# `WIP/new_tt` workflow. It re-estimates every branch length and reroots on the
# minimum-divergence branch. mpox divergence is counted in absolute mutations
# (`divergence_units: mutations`), and indels are excluded from the branch-length
# likelihood (`no_indels`), matching the pipeline's `treetime optimize` rule.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

reroot: "min-dev"
divergence_units: "mutations"
no_indels: true

configs.title: Tree cleanup: drop short and uninformative branches, collapse shared mutations (rsv/a/100).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-prune.schema.json

# Tree cleanup: drop short and uninformative branches, collapse shared mutations (rsv/a/100).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime prune --config data/rsv/a/100/prune.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/rsv/a/100/prune
#
# `prune` removes tree-builder artifacts before a downstream analysis: branches
# shorter than a threshold, branches carrying no mutation, and sibling branches
# in a polytomy that share identical mutations (regrouped under one edge).

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

collapse_short: 1.0e-6
collapse_empty: true
merge_shared_mutations: true

configs.title: Marginal reconstruction in the dense representation (rsv/a/2000).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-ancestral.schema.json

# Marginal reconstruction in the dense representation (rsv/a/2000).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime ancestral --config data/rsv/a/2000/ancestral-dense.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/rsv/a/2000/ancestral-dense
#
# The dense representation (`representation: dense`) keeps the state probabilities
# of every site at every node, so memory and time grow with the number of
# sequences times the genome length. The default (`auto`) chooses the sparse
# representation, which stores only the variable sites and is much faster on the
# same input. Use dense to compare the two representations, or as a heavy run on
# 2000 RSV-A genomes of 15 kb each.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

method_anc: "marginal"
representation: "dense"

configs.title: Marginal ancestral reconstruction on 2844 SARS-CoV-2 genomes (sc2/2844).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-ancestral.schema.json

# Marginal ancestral reconstruction on 2844 SARS-CoV-2 genomes (sc2/2844).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime ancestral --config data/sc2/2844/ancestral.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/sc2/2844/ancestral
#
# A large single-command run: marginal reconstruction treats every site
# independently, fits a GTR rate matrix from the data (the default
# `model: infer`), and maps nucleotide mutations onto the tree. The sparse
# representation (the default) stores only variable sites, which keeps a
# genome-length SARS-CoV-2 alignment tractable.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

method_anc: "marginal"

configs.title: Ancestral geography over 95 countries on 4500 SARS-CoV-2 genomes (sc2/4500).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-mugration.schema.json

# Ancestral geography over 95 countries on 4500 SARS-CoV-2 genomes (sc2/4500).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime mugration --config data/sc2/4500/mugration.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/sc2/4500/mugration
#
# The largest discrete-trait example. The cost of `mugration` grows with the
# number of nodes and with the square of the number of states, and this run has
# 4500 tips and 95 sampling countries. Sampling is very uneven between countries;
# `sampling_bias_correction` gives a rough factor of how many more transitions an
# even sample would show, and the run multiplies the fitted transition rate by it.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv.xz"
attribute: "country"

sampling_bias_correction: 2.0

# The default outputs, plus the probability of every country at every node.
confidence: true

configs.title: SARS-CoV-2 time tree with a skyline coalescent, 4500 genomes (sc2/4500).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-timetree.schema.json

# SARS-CoV-2 time tree with a skyline coalescent, 4500 genomes (sc2/4500).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime timetree --config data/sc2/4500/timetree.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/sc2/4500/timetree
#
# The largest tree among the examples: 4500 genomes of 30 kb each, with a
# compressed metadata table. The clock filter (`clock_filter`) excludes from the
# clock fit the tips whose root-to-tip distance is more than 3 interquartile
# distances from the regression line, for example tips with a wrong date or a
# contaminated sequence; this is stricter than the default of 4. The skyline
# coalescent (`coalescent: skyline`) fits a piecewise-linear history of the
# coalescent time scale Tc, and `confidence` adds the 90% intervals of the node
# dates, including the uncertainty of the estimated clock rate. `seed` makes the
# random order of the polytomy resolution reproducible.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv.xz"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

clock_filter: 3.0
coalescent: "skyline"
confidence: true
seed: 42

configs.title: Ancestral cluster of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates (tb/149).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-mugration.schema.json

# Ancestral cluster of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates (tb/149).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime mugration --config data/tb/149/mugration.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/tb/149/mugration
#
# A bacterial example. `mugration` reconstructs any discrete metadata column, not
# only geography: here the `cluster` column (16 states) of the 149 isolates. The
# alignment of this dataset holds only the 216 variable sites of the 4.4 Mb genome,
# and this run does not use it.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
attribute: "cluster"

# The default outputs, plus the probability of every cluster at every node.
confidence: true

configs.title: Marginal ancestral reconstruction with an inferred GTR model (zika/20).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-ancestral.schema.json

# Marginal ancestral reconstruction with an inferred GTR model (zika/20).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime ancestral --config data/zika/20/ancestral.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/zika/20/ancestral
#
# Marginal reconstruction treats every site independently and reports the
# maximum-likelihood ancestral state per node. It fits a GTR rate matrix from the
# data (the default `model: infer`) and writes it alongside the tree.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

method_anc: "marginal"

configs.title: Discrete ancestral geography ("mugration") over sampling country (zika/20).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-mugration.schema.json

# Discrete ancestral geography ("mugration") over sampling country (zika/20).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime mugration --config data/zika/20/mugration.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/zika/20/mugration
#
# `mugration` treats a discrete metadata column (here `country`) like a
# sequence character and reconstructs it on internal nodes, inferring a GTR
# model of transitions between states. `weights` supplies a prior on state
# equilibrium frequencies; `pc` is the pseudo-count that flattens the model.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
attribute: "country"

weights: "../country_weights.csv"
pc: 1.0

# The default outputs, plus the probability of every state at every node.
confidence: true

pipelines.title: Dengue build with a skyline coalescent and ancestral geography (dengue/2000).
Full three-step build on a real epidemic dataset (ebola/362).
Optimize then date, with a fixed clock rate defined once (flu/h3n2/200).
Seasonal influenza H3N2 build: optimize, reconstruct, date (flu/h3n2/500).
Nextstrain mpox build (clade IIb, hmpxv1), TreeTime part in one file (mpox/clade-ii/1000).
Nextstrain mpox build with ancestral geography, 2000 genomes (mpox/clade-ii/2000).
RSV-A time tree with resolved polytomies, then ancestral geography (rsv/a/2000).
SARS-CoV-2 branch-length optimization and ancestral reconstruction (sc2/2844).
Phylodynamics + phylogeography in one file: time tree, then ancestral geography (zika/20).
Zika virus spread in the Americas: time tree, then weighted ancestral geography (zika/86).
